No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

L1 supplies no explicit m,n or all-iterations invariant proving disjoint sigma-orbits; branch-B negation needs an infinite-separation construction that is itself the open EGPS core — exact repair: certified disjoint-orbit witness or proved invariant; imported domain-drift pattern from erdos1101 R001

the 43-row certificate is false: direct enumeration of pairs (a,b)≠(0,0) with 2^a·3^b ≤ 1000 gives 39 rows (b=0:9, b=1:9, b=2:7, b=3:6, b=4:4, b=5:3, b=6:1); also (0,1)↦3−1=2 is a prime row, the only empty-factorization row is (1,0)↦1; repair is a 39-row table, and Set.Infinite transfer remains bloc

circular/ equivalent-strength: "new primes must eventually appear" restates F(n)→∞; additionally quantifier slip — limit clause does not imply F(n)>n ∀ sufficiently large n; both contract clauses remain open, no candidate lemma was supplied beyond the tautology.

L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.
